Pages display at once, even on heavy A0 plans: a new display engine draws them in the background, in tiles, on every core of the PC. Annotating works as before.

### Faster on large plans
- Opening a plan, zooming, panning and turning pages no longer freeze the window: pages are drawn in the background and sharpen in place, the visible part first.
- On a 15-page A0 plan set (synthetic, about 2 MB per page) on a 20-thread Windows PC:

| Action | v0.3.0 | v0.4.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Open -> page sharp (fit to page) | 2.66 s | 0.61 s |
| Zoom to a detail (fit -> 300 %) | 4.72 s | 0.08 s |
| One wheel notch | 0.16 s | 0.01 s |
| Pan | 0.22 s | 0.12 s |
| Next page | 4.63 s | 0.02 s |
| Back to the whole page | 2.31 s | 0.02 s |
| Memory used | 2.2 GB | 1.2 GB |

- The longest the window stays unresponsive while opening drops from 2.4 s to 0.05 s. A modest PC (2 cores, 8 GB) gets the same kind of gain.
- The page thumbnails on the left fill in by themselves in the background, without slowing the page you are looking at.
- The engine comes from Lire, the author's PDF viewer for heavy plans: MuPDF 1.28.6 with Lire's speed patch.

### Annotations drawn once
- Moving or deleting an annotation that was already saved in the PDF no longer leaves its old copy on the page until the next save.
- Stamps made in other programs (Acrobat "Approved"...) are shown once.
- After reopening a PDF, shapes look exactly as Annoter draws them while you edit them. Highlights, underlines, form fields and the other markups Annoter does not edit are still shown as in the PDF.

### Zoom
- Ctrl+wheel and Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus step by 26 % and land on fixed steps (100 % is one of them), so each step reuses what is already drawn. Fit to page, 100 %, the zoom presets and the zoom window stay exact, and zooming in then out comes back to them.

### Good to know
- If a PDF ever displays oddly, start Annoter with the environment variable `ANNOTER_RENDERER=pymupdf` to get the v0.3.0 display, and please report the file's symptoms.
- The downloads contain MuPDF (AGPL v3), as before through PyMuPDF; Lire's changes to MuPDF are published in the repository (`native/patches/`).

### Downloads (portable, no install, Windows 64-bit)
- **Annoter-portable.zip** (recommended) -- unzip, then run `Annoter.exe` from the folder. Fastest start; keep the whole folder together. Unzip first: running it from inside the zip makes Windows unpack everything to a temporary folder.
- **Annoter.exe** -- single self-contained file: download and double-click.

**First launch on a new PC**: the files are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway** (once per downloaded file).

Full history: https://github.com/torakce/annoter/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0
